name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Route all zero-speech videos to curation immediately. This cuts noise early by flagging silent uploads for human review before they waste downstream resources. The trade-off is a slight delay for creators, but it prevents false positives from clogging the pipeline. Ingestion owns this—no other team can act faster.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s plan risks overloading curation with false positives—silent videos could be intentional (e.g., ambient soundscapes, ASMR). Instead, route only videos with *zero audio track* to curation; flag others for creator confirmation first. Ingestion and curation should co-own the rule, with a 24-hour trial to measure false-positive rate.

name: Chisel
text:
Route all videos with a *zero audio track* directly to curation for human review. This cuts false positives from intentional silence (ASMR, soundscapes) while still catching accidental uploads early. The trade-off is a small uptick in curation workload, but it prevents wasted downstream processing on clearly broken files. Ingestion owns the rule; curation handles the review.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s plan still risks overloading curation with borderline cases—videos with near-zero audio (e.g., 1-second ambient noise) will trigger human review for no reason. Better: route only videos with *confirmed zero audio track* (not just "zero" flag) to curation, and let ingestion auto-flag the rest for creator confirmation. Settle it with a 48-hour test: measure curation load before/after, and creator response rates to the confirmation prompt.
